dedupe_keys.name: data and code for when substitution boundaries decide a general criterion for comparing plastic recycling with waste to energy carbon capture

description: Tianjiao Cheng and Hiroshi Onoda publish a calculation chain for comparing plastic recycling with waste-to-energy carbon capture in Japan. Zenodo archives machine-readable data and code under MIT. The description covers seven routes for one tonne of post-consumer plastic, including mechanical and chemical recycling, incineration with energy recovery and incineration with carbon capture. It resolves a fossil-carbon balance in time and compares how substitution-credit boundaries change climate results. This model can inform waste-system or recycling-infrastructure scenario simulations. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this boundary-comparison package. Coverage is Japanese process and substitution assumptions, not direct measured emissions at every facility. A limitation is that the ranking may reverse when displaced virgin production or end-of-life treatment is defined differently; the paper’s chosen impulse-response function is another modelling choice. The archive was not downloaded, no life-cycle factors were checked and no radiative-forcing value was recalculated.
